directions.title: The Moving Cutting Room
directions.plan: Primary journey: enter through a model in motion fragmented by vertical pattern-piece frames; those rails survive the hero boundary, become the category/filter grid, and then reframe a nine-garment product atlas. One product can expand in place for colour, fabric, size, sold-out state and Add to bag without losing catalogue context. A magnified indigo weave then takes over the viewport and carries the same material into sizing, care, delivery, reviews and the closing 11 people / 1 Leeds shop / 4 factories / never sales proof. The bag is a persistent right drawer on desktop. Asset plan: generate or source one coherent representative editorial shoot covering all nine garment types plus two macro cloth details and one workshop analogue; label imagery as representative creative material, never verified inventory photography. Treat every image to one warm paper/oxblood/indigo grade. Mobile: convert the split hero into a swipeable three-frame crop with a compact sticky category strip; use a two-column product index, full-width inline product expander, and bottom-sheet bag; the weave handoff becomes a shorter scroll-linked crop rather than a pinned sequence. Implementation: React state already present remains canonical; reorganize into semantic sections and accessible controls, use CSS grid plus a small focused motion runtime only if the shared-frame handoff proves materially smoother than native scroll-linked animation. Normal motion synchronizes rail offsets, image crops and the weave zoom to scroll; reduced motion shows stable authored end frames with no pinning, parallax or smooth-scroll takeover. Exact source constants govern every garment fact, sold-out size, category count, size-chart row, care/shipping statement, review and shop fact; any tiny text rendered imperfectly in this generated concept image is not proposed copy. Uncertainty/cost: medium-high. The main risk is keeping the persistent framing expressive without obscuring sizes and buttons; prototype the hero-to-filter-to-first-product handoff at desktop and 390px before completing the route. Recommendation: strongest option because its continuity device is native to clothing construction, survives well beyond the hero, and leaves conventional buying patterns intact while still feeling authored in motion.

directions.title: One Long Rail
directions.plan: Primary journey: a full-bleed cast lineup introduces nine permanent wardrobe pieces; the category control is literally the rail beneath them. Scrolling advances a large horizontal runway while a stable commerce panel exposes exact price, colours, fabric, sizing and Add to bag. The selected garment dissolves into enlarging square pixels; those pixels reorganize into a blue-and-white information matrix for the full size chart, care, regional shipping and returns, three reviews, and the final 11 people / one Leeds shop / four factories / never sales statement. The bag is a touch-friendly bottom sheet on desktop and mobile. Asset plan: create a consistent flash-lit studio campaign with all nine representative garments, full-figure cutouts and fabric macros; no image is described as verified inventory. Use one cool neutral grade, hard shadows and a controlled ultramarine background so the set reads as one shoot. Mobile: the rail becomes deliberate horizontal snap browsing with one garment per screen, a persistent thumb-reachable filter, and a product detail sheet that expands upward; the pixel transition is reduced to a brief stepped wipe and the information matrix becomes accordion groups above the checkout sheet. Implementation: keep native vertical scroll around a pinned horizontal catalogue chapter, with one semantic product list beneath for accessibility and reduced motion; CSS masks/canvas sampling can drive the image-to-pixel handoff, while React owns filters, selected sizes, disabled sizes and bag totals. Normal motion uses one continuous x-progress value across hero, rail and pixel resolution; reduced motion removes pinning and renders a static vertical product list with direct anchors. Exact source constants govern every garment fact, sold-out size, category count, size-chart row, care/shipping statement, review and shop fact; any tiny text rendered imperfectly in this generated concept image is not proposed copy. Uncertainty/cost: high. Horizontal chapters can fight touch and keyboard navigation, so the central prototype must prove wheel, trackpad, swipe, focus and escape behavior before integration. Relative verdict: more immediately graphic and energetic than Direction A, but technically costlier and slightly less natural for comparing several garments quickly; choose it only if the bold digital runway is worth that interaction risk.
